why: rclrs's type discriminant, which is `rcl_interfaces`'s nine types PLUS a tenth, `Dynamic`, for a parameter allowed to change type. Ours is `ParameterType` (see `rust:ParameterType`), which mirrors `rcl_interfaces/msg/ParameterType` exactly and carries the dynamic-typing intent as a descriptor FLAG (`ParameterDescriptor::with_dynamic_typing`) rather than a tenth variant, so the enum stays byte-identical to what goes on the wire. What a user loses: a type-level distinction between a fixed and a dynamic parameter. AMENDED 2026-09-05 (phase-425): the NAME half of this pair is now `their-rename` on `rust:ParameterType` -- `rcl_interfaces/msg/ParameterType`, rclcpp and our own C all use our word, so rclrs is the outlier on the spelling. This row stays `declined` because it is not only a spelling: rclrs's enum carries a tenth variant, `Dynamic`, that we genuinely do not have, and a `their-rename` may not absorb a shape difference.
